title: Medicaid paid per enrolled resident: San Francisco against California
question: Do San Francisco billers take in more Medicaid money for each enrolled resident than the rest of the State, and is the gap growing?
finding: Billers registered in San Francisco were paid $2,174 per enrolled resident in 2023 for outpatient and professional services, 1.47 times the California figure of $1,482; in 2018 it was $2,071 against $1,150 (1.8 times). City government's own provider numbers took 51% of the San Francisco total in 2023.
how: Payments to billing numbers registered in each county were added by year of service and divided by the average number of residents certified eligible for Medi-Cal that year. California is all counties together.
limits: This compares where billers are registered, not where patients live. San Francisco hosts a university medical center, the City's own hospital and mental-health system and at least one national laboratory that bills for patients everywhere, so its figure is bound to be higher. Hospital stays, nursing homes and pharmacy are not in the file. 2024 is preliminary.
